title: Ruler-host simulation
statement: For every deterministic $m$-work-tape binary Turing machine $M$ with a finite state set $S$ and decidable state equality, there are a finite state set $Q$, a deterministic binary machine $H$ with $m+1$ work tapes, an injection $\mathrm{inj}:S\times\{0,1\}\to Q$, and a positive integer $C$ with the following property. Let $y,z$ be binary strings, let $\ell>0$ satisfy $|z|=\ell+|y|$ and $z$'s suffix after its first $\ell$ symbols equal $y$, and let the extra tape contain a ruler of $\ell$ ones from offset $-1$ through $\ell$, with head position $rp$. For any configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $y$ and bit $b$ indicating whether its input head is at position zero, and any time $t$, the host machine started on the paired input and configuration formed by shifting the input-head position by $\ell$, preserving the original tapes and output, and placing the ruler on its extra tape, reaches after some $t'$ with $t\le t'\le C(\ell+1)t$ the corresponding configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps, with the state encoded using a bit indicating whether that simulated input head is at zero. If $M$ has not halted before $t$, the host has not halted before $t'$; at every intermediate host time $u\le t'$, its original tapes and output agree with some simulated configuration at a time $v\le t$, the ruler tape is unchanged, and its ruler head remains in $[rp-1,rp+\ell]$. By time $t'$, each original tape has visited exactly the cells visited by the corresponding tape of $M$ through time $t$, and the ruler head has visited only cells in that same interval.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number m and a deterministic m-work-tape binary machine M
The state set S is finite with decidable equality
Binary strings y and z satisfy |z|=ℓ+|y|
The suffix of z after its first ℓ symbols is y
The ruler length ℓ is positive
The ruler tape agrees with the length-ℓ buffer tape at offsets −1 through ℓ
The initial input-head boundary bit b is true exactly when c's input position is zero
An arbitrary initial configuration c and time t
caveat: The conclusion's paired input and shifted configuration are described in words; the stated bounds and tape, output, state, and visited-cell conditions follow the formal statement.
